hero.alt: Green title card reading Does Laughing Break Wudu?

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham: Loud laughter invalidating wudhu
sources.supports: Hanafi four conditions; the three levels of laughter and their effects on wudu and prayer; the al-Tabarani narration from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari; Sharh al-Wiqayah reference.

sources.title: Jami at-Tirmidhi 74 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Hadith: no wudu except for a sound or a smell; at-Tirmidhi's hasan sahih grading.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 135 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Prayer of one who does hadath is not accepted until wudu; Abu Hurayrah's explanation of hadath as passing wind.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 137 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Do not leave the prayer unless one hears a sound or notices a smell.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 177 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: Al-Bukhari's chapter title: whoever considers wudu only from what comes out of the two passages, front and back.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 362 on Sunnah.com
sources.supports: One in doubt should not leave the mosque unless he hears a sound or perceives a smell.

sources.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:6 on Quran.com
sources.supports: The wudu verse, which names relieving oneself among things requiring purification.

review.notes: Re-read every capture retrieved 2026-10-29/30. The Hanafi conditions, three levels of laughter and the al-Tabarani narration are attributed to Darul Ifta Birmingham exactly as its page states; the narration is described as cited by them, not graded by us. No majority or other-madhab position is asserted because the checked sources do not state one: islamqa.info, seekersguidance.org and islamweb.net were outside the publisher's approved domains, and sunnah.com/bukhari:176 (which carries al-Hasan's chapter quote) returned HTTP 403, so they are not cited. Readers of other schools are directed to a scholar of their school. Funeral-prayer and outside-prayer statements follow directly from Birmingham's fourth condition. Hero generated locally with the meadow palette and inspected: 1200x630 legible title card, not duplicated in body. No app CTA; links /prayer-times and existing wudu guides.

claim_checks.claim: Hanafi ruling requires four conditions: adult, awake, loud laughter, prayer with ruku and sajdah
claim_checks.explanation: Page lists: 1. One is an adult 2. One is awake 3. One's laughter is loud 4. The prayer contains Ruku and Sajdah.

claim_checks.claim: Loud laughter the neighbour would hear breaks wudu and prayer; laughter audible only to oneself breaks prayer not wudu; smiling has no effect
claim_checks.explanation: Page describes loud laughing (wudhu and Salah break), laughing (prayer only invalidated, not wudhu) and smiling (no effect on validity), extracted from Sharhul Wiqayah.

claim_checks.claim: Hanafi evidence is al-Tabarani's narration from Abu Musa about a man falling into a hole and the Prophet ordering those who laughed to repeat wudu and prayer
claim_checks.explanation: Page quotes this narration as the evidence from hadith.

claim_checks.claim: There is no wudu except for a sound or a smell; at-Tirmidhi graded it hasan sahih
claim_checks.explanation: English text and Arabic note hadha hadithun hasanun sahih.

claim_checks.claim: Prayer of one who does hadath is not accepted until wudu; Abu Hurayrah explained hadath as passing wind
claim_checks.explanation: Hadith text and the Hadramawt man's question.

claim_checks.claim: One who imagines passing wind should not leave the prayer unless hearing a sound or noticing a smell
claim_checks.explanation: Abbad bin Tamim's uncle's question and the Prophet's reply.

claim_checks.claim: Muslim records the doubt hadith with not leaving the mosque unless sound or smell
claim_checks.explanation: Abu Huraira's narration in Sahih Muslim 362.

claim_checks.claim: Al-Bukhari's chapter title: whoever considers wudu only from what comes out of the two passages
claim_checks.explanation: Chapter 34 heading shown on the page, in English and Arabic, with hadith 177 under it.

claim_checks.claim: Quran 5:6 names relieving oneself among things requiring purification
claim_checks.explanation: Clear Quran translation: 'or have relieved yourselves'.
